title: From Sunlight to Starlight
caption: The Residencia under the night sky, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Starlight falls across flowing desert dunes and the Residencia, the residence building at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. Light pollution is practically absent at this remote site high in the Atacama Desert, so even after sunset the landscape is lit by the stars above. The only artificial lights for miles come from Paranal's own facilities, the telescopes and this building among them.

The Residencia is a true oasis. Astronomers and other staff who work at the observatory, which lies a short drive away and houses the Very Large Telescope, can come here after a long shift to escape the dry desert air, stroll through an indoor garden or take a swim in the pool.

The building is known for its distinctive design and its environmental innovations, including careful management of power and waste. A huge 35-metre glass dome on its roof lets natural starlight and sunlight pour into the building.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at Paranal. The source gives no camera or exposure details.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers far more starlight than the eye, so the stars and the starlit landscape look brighter here than they would in person.
